# Job Chapter 40 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 431v

---

**40:1** And-answered [vaya'an] YHWH [את] Iyyov and-said: **40:2** "Shall-a-faultfinder [ha-yasor] contend [yariv] with-the-Almighty [im-Shaddai]? Let-the-reprover [mokhiach] of-God [Eloah] answer [ya'anennu]."

**40:3** And-answered [vaya'an] Iyyov [את] YHWH and-said: **40:4** "Behold, I-am-small [qalloti]; what shall-I-answer-you [ashiveka]? My-hand [yadi] I-lay [samti] upon my-mouth [le-fi]. **40:5** Once [achat] I-have-spoken [dibbarti] and-I-will-not answer [ve-lo e'eneh]; and-twice [u-shtayim], and-I-will-not add [ve-lo osif]."

**40:6** And-answered [vaya'an] YHWH [את] Iyyov from-the-whirlwind [min-ha-se'arah] and-said: **40:7** "Gird [ezar] now your-loins [chalatsekha] like-a-man [ke-gaver]; I-will-ask-you [eshalkha] and-make-known [hodi'eni] to-me.

**40:8** Will-you-indeed [ha-af] annul [tafar] my-justice [mishpati]? Will-you-condemn-me [tarshi'eni] so-that you-may-be-righteous [lema'an titsddaq]? **40:9** And-if an-arm [zero'a] like-God's [ka-El] [is] to-you, and-with-a-voice [u-ve-qol] like-his [kamohu] you-can-thunder [tar'em]?

**40:10** Deck-yourself [adeh] now [with] majesty [ga'on] and-dignity [govahh], and-glory [hod] and-splendor [ve-hadar] put-on [tilbash]. **40:11** Scatter-abroad [hafets] the-overflowings of-your-anger [evrot appekha], and-look-at [u-re'eh] every proud-one [ge'eh] and-bring-him-low [ve-hashpilehu]. **40:12** Look-at [re'eh] every proud-one [ge'eh] — humble-him [hakhni'ehu]; and-tread-down [hadhokh] the-wicked [resha'im] in-their-place [tachtam]. **40:13** Hide-them [tomenem] in-the-dust [be-afar] together [yachad]; bind [chavosh] their-faces [peneihem] in-the-hidden-place [ba-tamon]. **40:14** And-even I will-praise-you [odekka], for your-right-hand [yeminekha] can-save-you [tosha lakh].

**40:15** Behold now Behemoth [behemot], which I-made [asiti] with-you [immakh]; grass [chatsir] like-the-ox [ka-baqar] it-eats [yokhel]. **40:16** Behold now, its-strength [kocho] [is] in-its-loins [be-motnav], and-its-power [ve-ono] in-the-muscles [bi-shrirei] of-its-belly [bitno]. **40:17** It-stiffens [yachpotz] its-tail [zenavo] like-a-cedar [ke-erez]; the-sinews [gidei] of-its-thighs [fachaddav] are-woven-together [yesoragu].

**40:18** Its-bones [atzamav] [are] tubes of-bronze [afiqei nechoshet]; its-limbs [geramav] [are] like-bars of-iron [ki-metil barzel]. **40:19** It [is] the-beginning [reshit] of-the-ways of-God [darkhei-El]; the-one-who-made-it [ha-osuhu] can-bring-near [yaggesh] his-sword [charbo].

**40:20** For the-mountains [harim] bear [yis'u] produce [bul] for-it, and-all the-beasts of-the-field [chayyat ha-sadeh] play [yesachequ] there. **40:21** Under the-lotus-plants [tachat tse'elim] it-lies [yishkav], in-the-covert [be-seter] of-the-reed [qaneh] and-the-marsh [u-vitsah]. **40:22** The-lotus-plants [tse'elim] cover-it [yesukkehu] [with] their-shade [tsillelo]; the-willows [arevei] of-the-brook [nachal] surround-it [yesuvbuhu].

**40:23** Behold, if-the-river [nahar] is-violent [ya'ashoq], it-is-not alarmed [lo yachpoz]; it-is-confident [yivtach] though the-Jordan [yarden] bursts [yagiyach] against its-mouth [el-pihu]. **40:24** Before-its-eyes [be-einav] can-one-take-it [yiqqachenu]? With-snares [be-moqshim] can-one-pierce [yiqqov] its-nose [appo]?"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — "I am small":** Hebrew *qalloti* — "I am insignificant/lightweight." This is Job's first response. It is not yet repentance but a recognition of his own smallness. He puts his hand over his mouth — not in shame but in overwhelm.

**v.15 — "Behemoth":** Hebrew *behemot* — grammatically the plural of *behemah* (beast/cattle), but used here as a singular, suggesting a superlative: "the beast par excellence." Its identity is debated: hippopotamus, elephant, mythological chaos creature, or a composite. The description fits the hippopotamus most closely (river habitat, grass-eating, powerful legs), but verse 17 ("tail like a cedar") does not match any known animal, suggesting mythological dimensions.

**v.19 — "the beginning of the ways of God":** Hebrew *reshit darkhei-El* — Behemoth is God's first or chief work. This language echoes Wisdom in Proverbs 8:22 (*reshit darkho*). Behemoth is presented as a primordial masterwork, not merely an animal.

**v.23 — "the Jordan":** The only geographical reference in the Behemoth passage. Some argue this localizes the creature; others see "Jordan" as a generic term for "rushing river."

*— EMET*
